=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- tests/test_implement_post_codex_recovery.py | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The mock gh handling of `label create|edit` (around lines 281-287) always succeeds, so branches in `guard_block_ensure_label` that detect "already exists", fall back to `gh label edit`, or retry the create have no behavioural test.
  WHY: If the "already exists" regex stopped matching gh's real message, every guard rejection on an existing label would fall into `gh_retry gh label create`; the tests would not notice. Only coverage is missing; I found no defect in the shipped branch logic.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The failed check `tests-promote-stall-and-review` is `tests/test_workflow_file_size_limit.py::test_interpolated_run_bodies_below_expression_guard`. It reports that run body at 19,821 characters, above the 18,000-character guard for run bodies containing `${{ }}`.
  WHY: The PR diff does not touch `update_workflows.yml`, so this PR did not cause it. `implement.yml` is not named in the failure, and the PR only adds comment lines and one `install` line to it. The check stays red, so this should be fixed on the integration branch. Fixing it means moving that step's body into `scripts/` with its `${{ }}` values passed through `env:` (unattended instructions §24). That is outside this issue's `files_touched`. Five of the six pass-1 reviewers (all but the one that returned no usable output) reported the same failure.
- scripts/implement_handle_guard_block.sh
  PROBLEM: The `2>/dev/null` redirects discard `gh_retry`'s `::warning::` and `::error::` lines.
  WHY: A retried or exhausted latch write then leaves no trace in the job log, only the later "unknown latch state" message. The old raw calls had the same redirect, so this is not a regression.
  Suggested minimal fix: Optionally send stderr to the log instead of `/dev/null` on the `gh_retry` paths.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/implement_handle_guard_block.sh: lines 9-66 (new `guard_block_ensure_label` function and its comment block); lines 89-90, 117-118, 391-393 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The function's source comment claims "only unexpected failures are retried" via `gh_retry gh label create ...`, but `gh label create` is a POST create — under the documented `gh_retry` policy POST creates get one attempt unless marked `--idempotent`. The retry-create branch therefore offers no actual backoff on a transient GitHub error during label creation; only the `gh_retry gh label edit` fallback (idempotent PUT) provides real retries.
  WHY: A brief GitHub 5xx/network blip while the very first `gh label create` is in flight causes the raw attempt to fail, then `gh_retry gh label create` also fails after one attempt (no backoff), then optionally `gh label edit` retries. The "retry" claim in the function header is not what the code does.
- scripts/implement_handle_guard_block.sh: lines 89-90, 117-118, 391-393; lines 86-90, 198-202, 391-393 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The blanket `2>/dev/null` redirects suppress `gh_retry`'s own `::warning::` retry diagnostics and the final `::error::` summary line.
  WHY: An exhausted label-creation retry chain leaves no `::warning::`/`::error::` trace. The warning echo that follows is the only signal, and it does not say which attempt count or HTTP status was hit.
- tests/test_implement_post_codex_recovery.py: lines 287-298 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The mock `gh` either succeeds (label create/edit) or fails outright (`MOCK_GH_ISSUE_EDIT_FAILURE`); no fake-gh mode emits the "already exists" message. The regex `'already[ _-]*exists|already_exists'` against real `gh label create` stderr, the `edit_existing=true` branch, and the retry-then-edit fallback therefore have no behavioural coverage.
  WHY: If the real `gh` CLI changes its "already exists" wording, the regex stops matching and every guard rejection falls into the raw `gh_retry gh label create` POST branch, paying ~15s of retry backoff sleeps before reaching `gh label edit`. The regression would not be caught by `tests/test_implement_post_codex_recovery.py`.
- scripts/implement_handle_guard_block.sh: lines 9-66 (the new `GUARD_BLOCK_*` block) vs the rest of the file | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The new top-of-file block uses TAB indentation for its `if`/`else`/`fi` bodies, while every other statement in the same script uses 2-space indentation.
  WHY: It does not fail; it is a stylistic inconsistency inside a single shell script.
- Requirement: The issue's CI expectation is that the PR lands green against the repo's CI gate.
  Expected change site: .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml (the "Commit and push updates" run body, currently 19,821 characters, exceeds the 18,000-character `${{ }}`-expression guard enforced by `tests/test_workflow_file_size_limit.py::test_interpolated_run_bodies_below_expression_guard`).
  Evidence of absence: The PR diff contains no change to `.github/workflows/update_workflows.yml`; the only workflow change is the `install -m 0644 scripts/gh_helpers.sh ...` line in `.github/workflows/implement.yml`. The CI failure log in `tests-promote-stall-and-review` (run 38209571673, job 114680493339) names the same `update-wrappers` step the other four reviewers flagged. Per `unattended_system_instructions.md` §24 / CLAUDE.md §27, a `run:` body of this size is a contract violation; the orchestrator project #7126 must address it before this PR's wave can complete.
